title: UW Market Data Document 1.0
description: A dated, attributable set of market observations (document profile `market-data-v1`, RFC 0022). It carries observations, not conclusions: no deal_id, no calculations, and no calc pack applies to it. Validating against this schema establishes that the observations are attributable — it establishes nothing about whether they are accurate, current, or representative.

document_id.description: Stable identity of this observation set, e.g. `md:phx-multifamily:2026-Q2`. Pinned by an RFC 0016 receipt's `inputs_provenance` so a computation is reproducible against exactly these observations.

as_of.description: Vintage of the observation set as a real calendar date. REQUIRED: an observation set with no as-of date is not attributable and MUST be refused rather than stored with the field blank. The pattern cannot reject an impossible date such as 2026-02-30 — an implementation MUST additionally verify the date exists, or it will silently roll forward to a day that never happened.

provider.description: Who published these observations. REQUIRED for the same reason as `as_of`: an unnamed source cannot be traced.

geo.description: Geography the observations describe. Matching against a deal is exact; normalizing place names is deliberately out of scope.

asset_class.description: Optional. When present, the set resolves only for deals of this asset class. Absent means it applies to any.

deal_id.description: MUST NOT be present. A market-data document is not an underwriting record, and carrying a deal_id is the cheapest way for it to be misread as one.

observations.description: The observations. Each `field_path` must be unique — two observations for one path would make resolution depend on array order.

field_path.description: A path a deal record could carry, as `<section>.<field>`. The section MUST be one FORMAT_SPEC Part IV registers, or an `x_` extension section (§ 4.21); this pattern checks the shape only, so an implementation MUST additionally check section membership. A market-data document MUST NOT introduce paths that do not exist in the section model.

value.description: The observed value. Rates are fractions, per the repo-wide convention: 0.0545 is 5.45%.

range.description: Optional dispersion. MUST satisfy low <= central <= high; a schema cannot express that ordering, so an implementation MUST check it.

basis.description: What the observation rests on — sample size, method, period. REQUIRED and non-empty: a number with no stated basis is an assertion, and this profile is for observations. Deliberately free text, because that is what providers actually publish; structuring it is noted as an open question in RFC 0022.

confidence.description: The provider's confidence, not the reader's. Promotion to an underwritten value does not raise it.
